challenged_claim: A bounded two-dimensional projected density, even together with bounded coordinate marginals, is sufficient receiver-side information to obtain a universal nonlinear quadratic density bound at a nonzero scalar pivot.
correction: False. For R>=e^2, rho_R=1_{1<=u<=R, |uv+R|<=1/(2 log R)} is a probability density with joint cap 1 and both coordinate marginal caps <=1. With independent X~Unif[0,1], Q=X^2+2UV has the fixed matrix spectrum {1,1,-1}, determinant -1, but p_Q(-2R)=(1/2)sqrt(log R)->infinity. Moreover E|2UV+2R|^{-1/2}=2sqrt(log R). This is not a QFORM counterexample because U,V are dependent and are not shown to be a product-law projection. It shows the projection-height abstraction loses the half-Riesz/product provenance needed for nonlinear integration.
partner_application: account04/B16 proves the genuine spectral-plane projection cap ||rho_Y||_infinity<=2 in its ruled/Pluecker endpoint theorem. The counterexample satisfies the stronger cap 1, so that partner cap alone cannot close the unpaid nonzero-pivot/two-sheet side; the product provenance behind it must be retained.
